50051-the-motor-boys-on-road-and-river-o.title: Racing To Save a Life
50051-the-motor-boys-on-road-and-river-o.creator: Clarence Young
50051-the-motor-boys-on-road-and-river-o.description: A book by Clarence Young. Sometimes, as you doubtless know, the simplest actions result in the most remarkable complications. When Jerry Hopkins picked up a lump of common-looking clay on some swamp land that his mother owned he had no idea what a strange series of events was to transpire from his simple act. Before he realized it he and his chums were involved in a strange secret, and they had set off on a trip that had, as its ultimate object, the saving of the life of Professor Snodgrass.

arxiv-2108-01364.title: Phase estimation of definite photon number states by using quantum circuits
arxiv-2108-01364.creator: Peyman Najafi, Ghasem Naeimi, Shahpoor Saeidian
arxiv-2108-01364.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Peyman Najafi, Ghasem Naeimi, Shahpoor Saeidian. We propose a method to map the conventional optical interferometry setup into quantum circuits. The unknown phase shift inside a Mach-Zehnder interferometer in the presence of photon loss is estimated by simulating the quantum circuits. For this aim, we use the Bayesian approach in which the likelihood functions are needed, and they are obtained by simulating the appropriate quantum circuits. The precision of four different definite photon-number states of light, which all possess six photons, is compared.

arxiv-2108-09863.title: Kippenhahn Varieties and the Weyl Calculus for Several Matrices I
arxiv-2108-09863.creator: Brian Jefferies
arxiv-2108-09863.description: Abstract . The paper reviews properties of the Weyl functional calculus for several operators and its relation to the generalised numerical range of n hermitian matrices. The support and singular support of the Weyl functional calculus for n n hermitian matrices are determined by Kippenhahn varieties in algebraic geometry. Dedicated to the memory of Alan McIntosh. 1.

arxiv-2204-03264.title: Deficit hawks: robust new physics searches with unknown backgrounds
arxiv-2204-03264.creator: Jelle Aalbers
arxiv-2204-03264.description: Abstract Searches for new physics often face unknown backgrounds, causing false detections or weakened upper limits. This paper introduces the deficit hawk technique, which mitigates unknown backgrounds by testing multiple options for data cuts, such as fiducial volumes or energy thresholds.

arxiv-2305-11797.title: Measuring Nonstabilizerness via Multifractal Flatness
arxiv-2305-11797.creator: Xhek Turkeshi, Marco Schirò, Piotr Sierant
arxiv-2305-11797.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xhek Turkeshi, Marco Schirò, Piotr Sierant. Universal quantum computing requires non-stabilizer (magic) quantum states. Quantifying the nonstabilizerness and relating it to other quantum resources is vital for characterizing the complexity of quantum many-body systems. In this work, we prove that a quantum state is a stabilizer if and only if all states belonging to its Clifford orbit have a flat probability distribution on the computational basis. This implies, in particular, that multifractal states are non-stabilizer.

arxiv-2307-03550.title: Notebook for the CheckThat! Lab at CLEF 2023
arxiv-2307-03550.creator: Ipek Baris Schlicht, Lynn Khellaf, Defne Altiok
arxiv-2307-03550.description: Abstract \changemarker This paper describes our submission for the subjectivity detection task at the CheckThat! Lab. To tackle class imbalances in the task, we have generated additional training materials with GPT-3 models using prompts of different styles from a subjectivity checklist based on journalistic perspective. We used the extended training set to fine-tune language-specific transformer models.

arxiv-2309-02450.title: Self-Supervised Video Transformers for Isolated Sign Language Recognition
arxiv-2309-02450.creator: Marcelo Sandoval-Castañeda 1 *, Yanhong Li 2, Diane Brentari 2, Karen Livescu 1, Gregory Shakhnarovich 1
arxiv-2309-02450.description: Abstract This paper presents an in-depth analysis of various self-supervision methods for isolated sign language recognition (ISLR). We consider four recently introduced transformer-based approaches to self-supervised learning from videos, and four pre-training data regimes, and study all the combinations on the WLASL2000 dataset.

arxiv-2310-19157.title: Accelerations of large inertial particles in turbulence
arxiv-2310-19157.creator: Yaning Fan, Cheng Wang, Linfeng Jiang, Chao Sun, Enrico Calzavarini
arxiv-2310-19157.description: Abstract Understanding the dynamics of material objects advected by turbulent flows is a long standing question in fluid dynamics. In this perspective article we focus on the characterization of the statistical properties of non-interacting finite-sized massive spherical particles advected by a vigorous turbulent flow.

arxiv-2312-06818.title: Bordism invariance of orientations and real APS index theory Thanks: This research was partly funded by a Simons Collaboration Grant on ‘Special Holonomy in Geometry, Analysis and Physics’. The author thanks Dominic Joyce for many discussions.
arxiv-2312-06818.creator: Markus Upmeier
arxiv-2312-06818.description: Abstract . We show that orientations and Floer gradings for elliptic differential operators can be propagated through bordisms. This is based on a new perspective on APS indices for elliptic boundary value problems over the real numbers. Several applications to moduli spaces of this new bordism-theoretic point of view will be given in the sequel.

arxiv-2401-04327.title: Implementation of space-division multiplexed entanglement-based quantum cryptography over multicore fiber
arxiv-2401-04327.creator: Evelyn A. Ortega, Jorge Fuenzalida, Krishna Dovzhik, Rodrigo F. Shiozaki, Juan Carlos Alvarado-Zacarias, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Martin Bohmann, Sören Wengerowsky, Rupert Ursin
arxiv-2401-04327.description: Abstract Quantum communication implementations require efficient and reliable quantum channels. Optical fibers have proven to be an ideal candidate for distributing quantum states. Thus, today’s efforts address overcoming issues towards high data transmission and long-distance implementations. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the secret key rate enhancement via space-division multiplexing using a multicore fiber.

arxiv-2412-01711.title: Towards Resource Efficient and Interpretable Bias Mitigation in Large Language Models
arxiv-2412-01711.creator: Schrasing Tong, Eliott Zemour*, Rawisara Lohanimit, Lalana Kagal
arxiv-2412-01711.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Schrasing Tong, Eliott Zemour*, Rawisara Lohanimit, Lalana Kagal. Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated their effectiveness in a wide range of applications, they have also been observed to perpetuate unwanted biases present in the training data, potentially leading to harm for marginalized communities. In this paper, we mitigate bias by leveraging small biased and anti-biased expert models to obtain a debiasing signal that will be added to the LLM output at decoding-time.

arxiv-2412-16126.title: Delays and Deferrals in Nuclear Waste Disposal: A Stochastic Analysis of Funding Shortfalls of Germany’s Waste Fund KENFO
arxiv-2412-16126.creator: Mahdi Awawda, Alexander Wimmers
arxiv-2412-16126.description: Abstract Germany is tasked ensuring the safe and final storage of high-level radioactive waste in a deep geological repository. Since 2022, the ambitious target year of 2031 to identify a suitable location for such a site has been deferred by most public actors.

arxiv-2502-20943.title: BadRefSR: Backdoor Attacks Against Reference-based Image Super Resolution Thanks: * This work was done at UESTC as a visiting student. † \dagger Corresponding author: Ji Guo (jiguo0524@gmail.com). This work is supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 62402087 and the
arxiv-2502-20943.creator: Xue Yang 1,3 1 Tao Chen 1 Lei Guo 1 Wenbo Jiang 1 Ji Guo 2 2 Yongming Li 3 Jiaming He 1,4 1
arxiv-2502-20943.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xue Yang 1,3 1 Tao Chen 1 Lei Guo 1 Wenbo Jiang 1 Ji Guo 2 2 Yongming Li 3 Jiaming He 1,4 1. Reference-based image super-resolution (RefSR) represents a promising advancement in super-resolution (SR). In contrast to single-image super-resolution (SISR), RefSR leverages an additional reference image to help recover high-frequency details, yet its vulnerability to backdoor attacks has not been explored.

arxiv-2507-23482.title: Orientable manifolds with nonzero dual Stiefel-Whitney classes of largest possible grading Thanks: 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification : 57R20, 57R19, 55S10.
arxiv-2507-23482.creator: Donald M. Davis
arxiv-2507-23482.description: Abstract . It is known that, for all n n , there exist compact differentiable orientable n n -manifolds with dual Stiefel-Whitney class w ¯ n − α ^ ​ ( n ) ≠ 0 \overline{w}_{n-\widehat{\alpha}(n)}\neq 0 , and this is best possible, but the proof is nonconstructive.

arxiv-2601-14636.title: Elastic lepton–proton two-photon exchange scattering: An exact HB χ \chi PT analysis including hadronic effects at NNLO
arxiv-2601-14636.creator: Rakshanda Goswami, Pulak Talukdar, Bhoomika Das, Udit Raha, Fred Myhrer
arxiv-2601-14636.description: Abstract We present an exact analytical evaluation of the two-photon exchange (TPE) correction to the elastic lepton–proton differential scattering cross section at low energies within the framework of heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory. Our analysis focuses on the kinematic regime relevant to the ongoing MUSE experiment, and we therefore restrict the intermediate states to the dominant elastic channel.

arxiv-2601-17040.title: FP-THD: Full page transcription of historical documents
arxiv-2601-17040.creator: Hala Neji, Javier Nogueras-Iso, Javier Lacasta, Miguel Ángel Latre, Francisco Javier García-Marco
arxiv-2601-17040.description: Abstract The transcription of historical documents written in Latin in XV and XVI centuries has special challenges as it must maintain the characters and special symbols that have distinct meanings to ensure that historical texts retain their original style and significance. This work proposes a pipeline for the transcription of historical documents preserving these special features.

arxiv-2602-05174.title: Total Variation Rates for Riemannian Flow Matching
arxiv-2602-05174.creator: Yunrui Guan, Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Shiqian Ma
arxiv-2602-05174.description: Abstract Riemannian flow matching (RFM) extends flow-based generative modeling to data supported on manifolds by learning a time-dependent tangent vector field whose flow-ODE transports a simple base distribution to the data law. We develop a nonasymptotic Total Variation (TV) convergence analysis for RFM samplers that use a learned vector field together with Euler discretization on manifolds.

arxiv-2602-11553.title: Perception-based Image Denoising via Generative Compression
arxiv-2602-11553.creator: Nam Nguyen, Thinh Nguyen, Bella Bose
arxiv-2602-11553.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Nam Nguyen, Thinh Nguyen, Bella Bose. Image denoising aims to remove noise while preserving structural details and perceptual realism, yet distortion-driven methods often produce over-smoothed reconstructions, especially under strong noise and distribution shift. This paper proposes a generative compression framework for perception-based denoising, where restoration is achieved by reconstructing from entropy-coded latent representations that enforce low-complexity structure, while generative decoders recover realistic textures via perceptual measures such as learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) loss and Wasserstein distance.

arxiv-2603-21753.title: Time to Get Closer: Longing for Care Ethics Under the Neoliberal Logic of Public Services
arxiv-2603-21753.creator: Rūta Šerpytytė

plos-pone-0001372.creator: Martina Buck, Mario Chojkier
plos-pone-0001372.description: PLOS ONE research article. In response to liver injury, hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation causes excessive liver fibrosis. Here we show that activation of RSK and phosphorylation of C/EBPβ on Thr217 in activated HSC is critical for the progression of liver fibrosis. Chronic treatment with the hepatoto

pmc-10617108.title: Research agenda for using artificial intelligence in health governance: interpretive scoping review and framework
pmc-10617108.creator: Maryam Ramezani, Amirhossein Takian, Ahad Bakhtiari, Hamid R Rabiee, Sadegh Ghazanfari, Saharnaz Sazgarnejad
pmc-10617108.description: BackgroundThe governance of health systems is complex in nature due to several intertwined and multi-dimensional factors contributing to it. Recent challenges of health systems reflect the need for innovative approaches that can minimize adverse consequences of policies. Hence, there is compelling evidence of a distinct outlook on the health ecosystem using artificial intelligence (AI).

pmc-10623811.title: Diversity of Thelazia spp. in domestic cattle from Romania: epidemiology and molecular diagnosis by a novel multiplex PCR
pmc-10623811.creator: Vlad-Dan Cotuțiu, Angela Monica Ionică, Teodora Dan, Cristina Daniela Cazan, Silvia Diana Borșan, Carla Andreea Culda, Marian Mihaiu, Călin Mircea Gherman, Andrei Daniel Mihalca
pmc-10623811.description: BackgroundThelaziosis is a neglected vector-borne disease caused by parasitic nematode worms of the genus Thelazia which affects various hosts. Limited attention has been given to ungulate-associated Thelazia species. Current diagnosis of thelaziosis and the identification/differentiation of species heavily relies on morphological features.

pmc-10660609.title: Inhibitory role of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells‐derived exosome in non‐small‐cell lung cancer: microRNA‐30b‐5p, EZH2 and PI3K/AKT pathway
pmc-10660609.creator: Tong Wu, Qi Tian, Ruiji Liu, Ke Xu, Shanshan Shi, Xiudi Zhang, Liming Gao, Xiaobo Yin, Shufeng Xu, Ping Wang
pmc-10660609.description: Exosomal microRNA (miRNA) exerts potential roles in non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The current study elucidated the role of miR‐30b‐5p shuttled by bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs)‐derived exosomes in treating NSCLC. Bioinformatics analysis was performed with NSCLC‐related miRNA microarray GSE169587 and mRNA data GSE74706 obtained for collection of the differentially expressed miRNAs and mRNAs.

pmc-10668753.title: Impact of Erythromycin as a Prokinetic on the Gut Microbiome in Children with Feeding Intolerance—A Pilot Study †
pmc-10668753.creator: Aravind Thavamani, Senthilkumar Sankararaman, Hilmi Al-Shakhshir, Mauricio Retuerto, Sujithra Velayuthan, Thomas J Sferra, Mahmoud Ghannoum, Gábor Ternák
pmc-10668753.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Studies have demonstrated that the gut microbiome changes upon exposure to systemic antibiotics. There is a paucity of literature regarding impact on the gut microbiome by long-term usage of erythromycin ethyl succinate (EES) when utilized as a prokinetic. Methods: Stool samples from pediatric patients with feeding intolerance who received EES (N = 8) as a prokinetic were analyzed for both bacteriome and mycobiome. Age-matched children with similar clinical characteristics but without EES therapy were included as controls (N = 20).

pmc-10747094.title: Design and Implementation of an Event-Driven Smart Sensor Node for Wireless Monitoring Systems
pmc-10747094.creator: Changrong Liu, Junjie Yang, Zhenghao Lu, Changnan Chen, Jiachou Wang, Dacheng Xu, Xinxin Li
pmc-10747094.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this paper, an event-driven wireless sensor node is proposed and demonstrated. The primary design objective is to devise a wireless sensor node with miniaturization, integration, and high-accuracy recognition ability. The proposed wireless sensor node integrates two vibration-threshold-triggered energy harvesters that sense and power a threshold voltage control circuit for power management, a microcontroller unit (MCU) for system control, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) environment data analysis and vibration events distribution, and a radio frequency (RF) digital baseband transmitter with IEEE

pmc-11333764.title: Development and validation of a nomogram of all-cause mortality in adult Americans with diabetes
pmc-11333764.creator: Xia Shen, Xiao Hua Zhang, Long Yang, Peng Fei Wang, Jian Feng Zhang, Shao Zheng Song, Lei Jiang
pmc-11333764.description: This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model of all-cause mortality risk in American adults aged ≥ 18 years with diabetes. 7918 participants with diabetes were enrolled from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999–2016 and followed for a median of 96 months. The primary study endpoint was the all-cause mortality.

pmc-11367835.title: Understanding stigma in the context of help-seeking for eating disorders
pmc-11367835.creator: Prudence L Wall, Daniel B Fassnacht, Esme Fabry, Anne E O’Shea, Catherine Houlihan, Kate Mulgrew, Kathina Ali
pmc-11367835.description: BackgroundStigma is a complex construct and its association with help-seeking among those experiencing eating disorders is not well understood. Rates of help-seeking are low for those with eating disorder symptoms and, therefore, determining the role of stigma and shame in this relationship is needed to help inform effective awareness campaigns aimed at improving prognostic outcomes.

pmc-11505529.title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Profiles of Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Northeastern Thailand
pmc-11505529.creator: Sumontha Chaisaeng, Nattamol Phetburom, Pachara Kasemsiri, Nuntiput Putthanachote, Naowarut Wangnadee, Parichart Boueroy, Anusak Kerdsin, Peechanika Chopjitt
pmc-11505529.description: The global emergence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae presents a significant public health threat and complicates antibiotic treatment for infections. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae in a clinical setting, analyze their antimicrobial susceptibility profiles, and characterize both phenotypic and genetic determinants.

pmc-11653004.title: Effects of incentivising dialysis facilities on peripheral arterial disease care in patients undergoing haemodialysis: a claims-based cohort study
pmc-11653004.creator: Yasunori Suzuki, Masao Iwagami, Sayuri Shimizu, Atsushi Goto
pmc-11653004.description: BackgroundPeripheral arterial disease (PAD) occurs frequently in patients undergoing dialysis, but early intervention for PAD may not be fully implemented. We evaluated the effects of financially incentivising dialysis facilities that provided early detection and management of PAD on outcomes of PAD care.

pmc-12473582.title: Arabinoxylan-Based Bioplastic from Wheat Bran: A Promising Replacement for Synthetic Plastics
pmc-12473582.creator: Md Abdur Rahim Badsha, Michael Kjelland, Chad Ulven, Khwaja Hossain, Nuno Gama, Alessandra Lorenzetti
pmc-12473582.description: The milling process of wheat annually generates over 150 million tons of wheat bran (WB), which has significant potential for bioplastic production. However, the production of bioplastics from these resources has never been explored until now. Wheat bran (WB) polymer was evaluated for its potential as an environmentally friendly biodegradable plastic, exhibiting a tensile strength of 2.

pmc-12542134.title: The association between glycated hemoglobin and intraocular inflammatory factors in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy
pmc-12542134.creator: Jun Liu, Miao Yu, Jingyu Yan, Wei Chen, Pei Zhang, Yuchen Wang, Huijin Chen, Jinping Hu
pmc-12542134.description: PurposeThis study explored the correlation between Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and intraocular inflammatory cytokines in proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) patients, aiming to provide evidence for PDR prevention and management.MethodsThis was a cross-sectional study involving 100 patients and 100 eyes diagnosed with PDR. All patients were collected demographic characteristics, HbA1c, and history of chronic diseases at baseline.

pmc-12974760.title: Femoral head fractures: anatomy, diagnosis and management
pmc-12974760.creator: Olivia Ann Dunseath, Ibrahem Al-Obaidi, Luca Ignatius, Branavan Rudran, Chris Jordan
pmc-12974760.description: Femoral head fractures are complex and severe injuries, usually associated with hip dislocation. They typically result from high-energy trauma. Therefore, a low index of suspicion is required for diagnosis in these contexts. Initial presentation can vary depending on coexisting injuries but is typically an emergency and requires immediate reduction of the joint. Delays result in worse outcomes for patients.

pmc-13076852.title: Updated Viloxazine Pharmacology: Experiments Establish Norepinephrine Transporter Occupancy and Serotonin 5-HT2C, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT7 Receptor Binding at Therapeutically Relevant Concentrations
pmc-13076852.creator: Jennie Garcia-Olivares, Brittney Yegla, Jennifer Koch, Chungping Yu, Jonathan Rubin
pmc-13076852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and ObjectivesViloxazine, which has been used to treat depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), has been termed a moderate-affinity, selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor based on high selectivity for norepinephrine relative to serotonin and dopamine transporters. However, accumulated research suggests a more complex mechanism of action, based on studies showing activity at serotonin 5-HT2C, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT7 receptors, as well as findings that viloxazine increases extracellular serotonin (along with norepinephrine and dopamine) in the rat prefrontal cortex.

pmc-13252290.title: Effect of AI-powered patient management systems in dental clinics
pmc-13252290.creator: S Mohammed Harris, Revanth S Soonthodu, Saloni Bharti, Maneesha Das, Christina Sarah James, K Aadisha
pmc-13252290.description: Dental clinics frequently experience operational inefficiencies due to fragmented data systems and manual administrative processes. Therefore, it is of interest to evaluate the impact of AI-powered patient management systems on workflow efficiency, data accuracy and patient satisfaction across five clinics. Appointment scheduling time reduced from 9.6 ± 2.4 to 3.2 ± 1.1 minutes, billing errors declined from 12.5 ± 3.

pmc-13457875.title: Quantitative assessment of occlusal function before and after extraction of unilateral impacted mandibular third molars using the TeeTester occlusal analyzer
pmc-13457875.creator: Shengwen Liu, Haojie Chen, Mingle Wu, Xi Chen, Shan Shen
pmc-13457875.description: BackgroundImpacted teeth of mandibular third molars have been associated with disruptions in full-mouth occlusal force distribution, potentially affecting mandibular movement, masticatory muscle activity, and temporomandibular joint function. The present investigation employed the TeeTester occlusal analyzer to obtain quantitative data on the occlusal characteristics associated with impacted mandibular third molars (IM3Ms), both prior to and following surgical extraction.

taylor-eleusinian-bacchic-mysteries-1790.description: Taylor's pioneering dissertation on the Greek mystery rites — the work that introduced the Eleusinian mysteries to English readers and founded modern pagan esoteric scholarship.
